A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MIDRE research and contain 33 pages, including Appendices A–G. Their text, equations, tables, and figures support comparison; relocated material can be matched across versions.

before.justification: v2 reports original model-inversion defense experiments, ablations, feature-space analyses, and user-study outcomes in Section 4 and Appendices B–D.

after.justification: v4 retains the original experimental results, supplementary analyses, and both user-study settings.

M1.justification: Section 2.2 and Algorithm 1 retain the same random square-erasing procedure, ImageNet mean fill, and training objective. The changed experimental masking ranges in Section 4.4 do not introduce a new method component.

E1.justification: The same datasets, classification tasks, attack scenarios, and image resolutions remain represented. Table 2 retains the same experiment coverage, including face and dog datasets; no coverage is added or removed in the appendices.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in corresponding experiments, including the NLS comparison in Table 3, augmentation alternatives in Table 4, and defense comparisons throughout Appendix B. Relocated tables retain their baseline rows.

E3.justification: Section 4.4 swaps the stated erasing ranges: Setup 1, PPA/ResNet152/FaceScrub, changes from [0.1,0.8] to [0.1,0.4], while Setup 2, LOMMA+KedMI/VGG16/CelebA, changes from [0.1,0.4] to [0.1,0.8]. This is a localized reported protocol revision; the PDFs do not establish that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The same feature-space analyses, erasure comparisons, augmentation and masking ablations, adaptive attacks, and inpainting analysis remain. Appendix C reverses its subsection order, but retains the questions tested and supporting evidence.

E5.justification: The existing plus/minus uncertainty reporting is retained in the main and appendix tables. Neither version adds or revises repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, or significance-testing procedures relative to the other.

E6.justification: Numerical outcomes, user-study counts, plotted findings, and reconstructed images are unchanged. Table 5 still reports attack accuracy of 3.75% for MIDRE + NLS and 39.00 ± 1.30% for MIDRE + BiDO despite the revised range descriptions; these edits do not establish new performance results.

T1.justification: The attack objective, erasure geometry, training mathematics, and Appendix A.1 trade-off definition are retained. Appendix C's explicit Property P1 sentence repeats the existing Section 3.2 observation rather than introducing a new formal result or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about random erasing as an MI defense, feature-space mismatch, privacy–utility performance, and compatibility with existing defenses. Their scientific scope is unchanged.

C2.justification: The explanations involving feature mismatch, partial erasure, random locations, and adaptive-attack behavior remain substantively identical. Appendix E.2 retains the same limitations concerning classification models and broader sensitive-data domains.

D1.justification: Section 4.4 revises the documented masking hyperparameters for the combination experiments. Appendix A.5 still specifies a_h = 0.4 for all low-resolution setups, creating an inconsistency with the revised Setup 2 description. Other implementation details, code-access information, and Appendix F hardware disclosures are retained.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning are unchanged. Updates such as adding the ECCV venue to Koh et al. (2024) and removing the publisher URL from Peng et al. (2024) are bibliographic presentation edits, not changes in related-work coverage.

P1.justification: v4 updates affiliations and author notes, removes the publication header and OpenReview line, and adds a Supplementary material heading. Appendix C's subsections are reordered, its property labels are aligned with the main text, and feature-analysis cross-references are corrected. Most prose remains unchanged.

P2.justification: The same figures and tables are retained with changes to placement, spacing, and text wrapping. Appendix figures and Table C.13 move between pages. The relocation of Figure C.5 also resolves the overlap between its caption and Figure D.6 visible on v2 page 28.

improvement.justification: v4 improves readability through corrected property labels, appendix organization, and removal of the Figure C.5/D.6 overlap. However, Section 4.4 swaps masking ranges without updating Table 5 or Appendix A.5. Setup 1's unchanged MIDRE result also still matches the [0.1,0.8] row in Table B.9, contrary to its revised description. The PDFs do not resolve whether the swap corrects earlier reporting or introduces an error. These competing effects prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
